text: Proposed future syntax rules, **not yet project-enforced**: in new JavaScript, use `const`/`let` rather than `var`; prefer `===`/`!==` unless a deliberate nullish/coercion check has a reason; use optional chaining only when absence is valid, not to hide a broken invariant; name every new async test task; keep one failure condition per assertion when separate values aid diagnosis; use meaningful boolean names; use a JSDoc block for exported/public functions and a short `//` comment for a surprising local reason; write CSS in logical properties and reuse existing design tokens before literals; prefer CSS classes to inline presentation except where Gecko chrome behavior requires inline style. Apply only to new or edited lines; do not demand mechanical rewrites of untouched legacy files. Review D302333 illustrates a platform-specific inline-style exception. Do not infer a global C++ or Rust naming rule from these commits; their local conventions and formatters govern.
